subject: Can "normal_lpdf" give a positive result? Strange error

messages.author: 7a97c986864bf6d6
messages.subject: Can "normal_lpdf" give a positive result? Strange error
parts:
In attempting to calculate the probability of a 2D number to belong to a 2D cluster I am using normal_lpdf

transformed parameters{
for(i in 1:I) {
vector<upper=0>[2] cluster_log[G*P];
cluster_log[i,1] = normal_lpdf(.. | .., ..);
cluster_log[i,2] = normal_lpdf(.. | .., ..);
}
}

How is possible that normal_lpdf gives a positive result?

ERROR: cluster_log[k0__][1] is 1.45791, but must be less than or equal to 0" 

Thanks.

messages.author: 743bbacc59f4b25f
messages.subject: Re: Can "normal_lpdf" give a positive result? Strange error
parts:
On Tuesday, April 11, 2017 at 3:34:25 AM UTC-4, Ste wrote:
How is possible that normal_lpdf gives a positive result?

Since a PDF is the slope of the CDF, it can go above 1 for a subset of the parameter space, in which case the log is positive. See for example

dnorm(0, mean = 0, sd = 0.25, log = TRUE) # 0.467

Ben

messages.author: a236d3d356ca53fd
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Re: Can "normal_lpdf" give a positive result? Strange error
parts:
Slightly longer answer: you need to understand the difference between probability density and probability mass. Density can be get values larger than 1, while probabilities are constrained to be less than or equal to 1.
See more, e.g., in https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Probability_density_function

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Can "normal_lpdf" give a positive result? Strange error
parts:
You can in many cases look at posterior probabilities of mixture
responsibilities even for continuous outcomes. That may be what
you want and it's explained in the manual chapter on mixtures (or
the chapter on clustering).

We have to just guess when people send us fragments with no
explanation of their goals.

- Bob
